title: RQ-D3 with a heralded filter: three fresh merge levels, four hard caps, O(2^(13n/100)) work, O(n^4) copies, tolerance 1-1/(10^64-3)^4

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the ONE RQ-D3 algorithm and exact parameter rule of proof.md, with every source acquisition served by the heralded filter FILTER of heralded.md (the identity when copies carry no herald; literal raw-acquisition cutoff D*Qcap, D=(10^64-3)^4, Qcap=131072(n+1)^3K the base's own hard cap on acquired originals, proof.md Section 4), recover the full s for the clean problem and under the heralded malformed-copy model of claim 5 (heralded.md Lemmas H.1-H.2 and Theorem H.3; the clean problem is the no-replacement strategy of ModelM, whose unflagged guarantee is proved in proof.md but not claimed) with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3. On EVERY branch including all retries, rejected or discarded copies, failed attempts, wrong numerical-label branches, partial inputs and any cutoff, its total charged sequential work T, including every FILTER herald read, reset and raw-counter step (charged outside the base's caps, heralded.md Theorem H.3), is O(2^((13/100)n)). This is its full uniform bit-length envelope for n>=2, with the SAME all-n protocol at n=1 having finite costs absorbed by absolute constants. Its exact envelope growth index is 1. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes. This holds jointly with the other three resources and the joint heralded fractional-tolerance declaration 1-1/(10^64-3)^4 of claim 5 for this same algorithm/configuration.

If at most floor(epsilon(n) Q') of the Q' raw acquired copies are malformed on every branch, then for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ the output equals the entire s with probability at least 1-2^-8 > 2/3, jointly with the four resource bounds of claims 0-3 on every execution branch (heralded.md Lemmas H.1-H.2 and Theorem H.3, using the clean-problem success proof of proof.md Sections 3-8). With no herald (the clean problem) the algorithm is exactly RQ-D3. The unflagged ModelM guarantee epsilon = 1/(134217728*n^3) of the baseline remains proved in proof.md but is not claimed here. No tolerance of undetectable corruption is claimed here.

structured.error_model: Heralded malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires on an execution branch, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Each acquired copy consists of an (n+1)-qubit register of the ideal copy's shape together with one classical herald bit f delivered with it. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed. A well-formed copy has f = 0 and its register is a fresh copy of rho_s, in tensor product with every other system (earlier copies, the adversary's system and the algorithm's registers). A malformed copy has f = 1 and its register is in an arbitrary state chosen by the adversary, possibly entangled with the adversary's private system and with other malformed copies. On every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. The herald is always correct, so malformation is detectable (an erasure-type error); its timing, its number within the promise and the malformed register contents are adversarial. In the clean problem no herald is supplied and every copy is well-formed. No source control, purification access or preparation inverse is supplied.
